domain: Social Ontology / Power Dynamics / Collective Memory
topic_summary: Analysis of a narrative depicting a labor warren where bodies develop hybrid mineral tissue from environmental exposure. The story traces how a distributed memory practice emerges through physical contact with stone infrastructure, creating an alternative kinship register that operates beneath institutional surveillance while the stone itself functions as an unrecognized archive of the discarded.

key_entities: Warren collective (labor bodies developing hybrid tissue)
Archivist (external observer detecting but not decoding signal elevation)
Young core (body at threshold learning new contact practice)
key_tensions: Institutional disposal logic vs emergent preservation practice (audit removes bodies; stone retains presence)
Surveillance legibility vs substrate communication (compliance scan reads bodies; bodies read stone)
Individual memory capacity vs distributed substrate storage (elder cannot hold all names; stone holds simultaneously)
key_mechanisms: Contamination threshold enforcement (audit cycle removes bodies at 12% progression)
Palm-to-stone contact practice (bodies press against ferrocrete, receive layered frequency)
Imitative distribution (practice spreads through observation without instruction)
Signal propagation through substrate (stone carries accumulated presence laterally and upward)
key_absences: No institutional recognition of stone as active carrier (Archivist detects signal but defers decoding)
No explicit coordination of contact practice (distribution happens through body-reading, not discussion)
